241| 			"to request completion choices for the specified command-line.", ShellCompRequestCmd),
242| 		Run: func(cmd *Command, args []string) {
243| 			finalCmd, completions, directive, err := cmd.getCompletions(args)
244| 			if err != nil {
245| 				CompErrorln(err.Error())
246| 				// Keep going for multiple reasons:
247| 				// 1- There could be some valid completions even though there was an error
248| 				// 2- Even without completions, we need to print the directive
249| 			}
250| 
251| 			noDescriptions := cmd.CalledAs() == ShellCompNoDescRequestCmd
252| 			if !noDescriptions {
253| 				if doDescriptions, err := strconv.ParseBool(getEnvConfig(cmd, configEnvVarSuffixDescriptions)); err == nil {
254| 					noDescriptions = !doDescriptions
255| 				}
256| 			}
257| 			noActiveHelp := GetActiveHelpConfig(finalCmd) == activeHelpGlobalDisable
258| 			out := finalCmd.OutOrStdout()

260| 				if noActiveHelp && strings.HasPrefix(comp, activeHelpMarker) {
261| 					// Remove all activeHelp entries if it's disabled.
262| 					continue

264| 				if noDescriptions {

267| 				}

270| 				// This is needed if a description contains a linebreak.
271| 				// Otherwise the shell scripts will interpret the other lines as new flags
272| 				// and could therefore provide a wrong completion.
273| 				comp = strings.SplitN(comp, "\n", 2)[0]

276| 				// of a trailing tab when there are no description following it.

283| 				fmt.Fprintln(out, comp)

287| 			// The directive integer must be that last character following a single colon (:).
288| 			// The completion script expects :<directive>
289| 			fmt.Fprintf(out, ":%d\n", directive)

291| 			// Print some helpful info to stderr for the user to understand.
292| 			// Output from stderr must be ignored by the completion script.
293| 			fmt.Fprintf(finalCmd.ErrOrStderr(), "Completion ended with directive: %s\n", directive.string())

316| func (c *Command) getCompletions(args []string) (*Command, []Completion, ShellCompDirective, error) {
317| 	// The last argument, which is not completely typed by the user,
318| 	// should not be part of the list of arguments

321| 	// backing array (which may be os.Args) when later appending "--".
322| 	trimmedArgs := make([]string, len(args)-1)
323| 	copy(trimmedArgs, args[:len(args)-1])

325| 	var finalCmd *Command
326| 	var finalArgs []string
327| 	var err error
328| 	// Find the real command for which completion must be performed
329| 	// check if we need to traverse here to parse local flags on parent commands
330| 	if c.Root().TraverseChildren {
331| 		finalCmd, finalArgs, err = c.Root().Traverse(trimmedArgs)

333| 		// For Root commands that don't specify any value for their Args fields, when we call
334| 		// Find(), if those Root commands don't have any sub-commands, they will accept arguments.

351| 	// These flags are normally added when `execute()` is called on `finalCmd`,
352| 	// however, when doing completion, we don't call `finalCmd.execute()`.

354| 	// has not disabled flag parsing; if flag parsing is disabled, it is up to the
355| 	// finalCmd itself to handle the completion of *all* flags.

358| 		finalCmd.InitDefaultVersionFlag()
359| 	}

361| 	// Check if we are doing flag value completion before parsing the flags.

378| 	}
379| 
380| 	realArgCount := finalCmd.Flags().NArg()
381| 	if newArgCount > realArgCount {
382| 		// don't do flag completion (see above)
383| 		flagCompletion = false
384| 	}
385| 	// Error while attempting to parse flags
386| 	if flagErr != nil {
387| 		// If error type is flagCompError and we don't want flagCompletion we should ignore the error
388| 		if _, ok := flagErr.(*flagCompError); !ok || flagCompletion {
389| 			return finalCmd, []Completion{}, ShellCompDirectiveDefault, flagErr
390| 		}
391| 	}
392| 
393| 	// Look for the --help or --version flags.  If they are present,
394| 	// there should be no further completions.
395| 	if helpOrVersionFlagPresent(finalCmd) {
396| 		return finalCmd, []Completion{}, ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp, nil
397| 	}
398| 
399| 	// We only remove the flags from the arguments if DisableFlagParsing is not set.
400| 	// This is important for commands which have requested to do their own flag completion.
401| 	if !finalCmd.DisableFlagParsing {
402| 		finalArgs = finalCmd.Flags().Args()
403| 	}
404| 
405| 	if flag != nil && flagCompletion {
406| 		// Check if we are completing a flag value subject to annotations
407| 		if validExts, present := flag.Annotations[BashCompFilenameExt]; present {
408| 			if len(validExts) != 0 {
409| 				// File completion filtered by extensions
410| 				return finalCmd, validExts, ShellCompDirectiveFilterFileExt, nil
411| 			}
412| 
413| 			// The annotation requests simple file completion.  There is no reason to do
414| 			// that since it is the default behavior anyway.  Let's ignore this annotation
415| 			// in case the program also registered a completion function for this flag.
416| 			// Even though it is a mistake on the program's side, let's be nice when we can.
417| 		}
418| 
419| 		if subDir, present := flag.Annotations[BashCompSubdirsInDir]; present {
420| 			if len(subDir) == 1 {
421| 				// Directory completion from within a directory
422| 				return finalCmd, subDir, ShellCompDirectiveFilterDirs, nil
423| 			}
424| 			// Directory completion
425| 			return finalCmd, []Completion{}, ShellCompDirectiveFilterDirs, nil
426| 		}
427| 	}

429| 	var completions []Completion
430| 	var directive ShellCompDirective

432| 	// Enforce flag groups before doing flag completions
433| 	finalCmd.enforceFlagGroupsForCompletion()

451| 					strings.Contains(flag.Value.Type(), "Array") ||

463| 			// non-inherited flags.

108|     local shellCompDirectiveNoSpace=%[4]d
109|     local shellCompDirectiveNoFileComp=%[5]d
110|     local shellCompDirectiveFilterFileExt=%[6]d
111|     local shellCompDirectiveFilterDirs=%[7]d
112|     local shellCompDirectiveKeepOrder=%[8]d

114|     local lastParam lastChar flagPrefix requestComp out directive comp lastComp noSpace keepOrder
115|     local -a completions

117|     __%[1]s_debug "\n========= starting completion logic =========="
118|     __%[1]s_debug "CURRENT: ${CURRENT}, words[*]: ${words[*]}"

121|     # We need to trigger completion from the $CURRENT location, so we need

124|     words=("${=words[1,CURRENT]}")
125|     __%[1]s_debug "Truncated words[*]: ${words[*]},"

143|         # We add an extra empty parameter so we can indicate this to the go completion code.

103| }

107|     local shellCompDirectiveError=%[3]d
108|     local shellCompDirectiveNoSpace=%[4]d
109|     local shellCompDirectiveNoFileComp=%[5]d
110|     local shellCompDirectiveFilterFileExt=%[6]d
111|     local shellCompDirectiveFilterDirs=%[7]d
112|     local shellCompDirectiveKeepOrder=%[8]d

114|     local lastParam lastChar flagPrefix requestComp out directive comp lastComp noSpace keepOrder
115|     local -a completions

117|     __%[1]s_debug "\n========= starting completion logic =========="
118|     __%[1]s_debug "CURRENT: ${CURRENT}, words[*]: ${words[*]}"

121|     # We need to trigger completion from the $CURRENT location, so we need

125|     __%[1]s_debug "Truncated words[*]: ${words[*]},"

171|     fi
172|

174|     __%[1]s_debug "completions: ${out}"
175|     __%[1]s_debug "flagPrefix: ${flagPrefix}"
176|

178|         __%[1]s_debug "Completion received error. Ignoring completions."
179|         return
180|     fi
181| 
182|     local activeHelpMarker="%[9]s"
183|     local endIndex=${#activeHelpMarker}
184|     local startIndex=$((${#activeHelpMarker}+1))
185|     local hasActiveHelp=0

261|         fi

276|             return 0
277|         else
278|             __%[1]s_debug "_describe did not find completions."
279|             __%[1]s_debug "Checking if we should do file completion."
280|             if [ $((directive & shellCompDirectiveNoFileComp)) -ne 0 ]; then
281|                 __%[1]s_debug "deactivating file completion"
282| 
283|                 # We must return an error code here to let zsh know that there were no
284|                 # completions found by _describe; this is what will trigger other
285|                 # matching algorithms to attempt to find completions.
286|                 # For example zsh can match letters in the middle of words.
287|                 return 1

291|

293|                 # last command, or else we must store its result to return it.
294|                 _arguments '*:filename:_files'" ${flagPrefix}"

296|         fi
297|     fi
298| }

302|     _%[1]s
